concepts.title: Weather versus Climate
concepts.definition: Weather is the atmosphere's state right now, while climate is the average pattern of weather of a region over many years; Chennai may have a cool day, but its climate stays coastal and warm.
concepts.formula: climate = average of weather over many years
concepts.key_idea: Climate is the habit, weather the mood: one place, two time scales.

concepts.title: Why India's Climate Is So Diverse
concepts.definition: Latitude, the seas on three sides, the mountains in the north and the monsoon winds together make India's climate swing from Himalayan snow to equatorial warmth and from desert dryness to Meghalaya's rain.
concepts.key_idea: One country spans many climates because place and wind shape each region differently.

concepts.title: The Seasons of India
concepts.definition: Indian climate runs in seasons: a cold season, a hot season, the advancing monsoon that brings most rain, and the retreating monsoon with its storms, each changing farm work and festivals.
concepts.key_idea: The monsoon is the heart of the Indian year: seasons are counted by its coming and going.

concepts.title: Climate Change and Preventive Measures
concepts.definition: Climate is not fixed: human activity is warming the planet, bringing harsher heat, irregular rain and storms; the chapter asks groups to discuss preventive measures, from saving energy to planting trees.
concepts.key_idea: Climate change is a shared problem: small preventive acts, multiplied by millions, blunt it.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why does the same sun give different climates to Ladakh and Kerala?

solution_template.explain: Ladakh lies high in the rain shadow of the Himalayas; Kerala is low, coastal and near the equator.
Altitude and distance from the sea bend temperature and rain, so the same sun yields two climates.
